acceptance_criteria: Given a visitor opens sign-in, when the page renders, then it shows a bordered panel headed “Sign in”, labeled “Email address” and “Password” inputs with “name@example.com” and masked “********” placeholders, a blue underlined “Forgot password?” link below the password input, a dark rectangular “Sign in” button below the link, and a muted “No account? requirements.statement: Start a password-reset request from the sign-in recovery link.
acceptance_criteria: Given the sign-in page is displayed, when the visitor follows “Forgot password?”, then they reach the password-reset request flow.

requirements.statement: Return an account-existence-independent response to password-reset requests.
acceptance_criteria: Given otherwise equivalent reset requests for an existing and a nonexistent account, when they are submitted, then their user-visible responses are identical.

Given reset requests while an existing account is at its request limit, when those and otherwise equivalent requests for a nonexistent account are submitted, then the user-visible responses remain identical and do not disclose account existence or throttling state.

requirements.statement: Limit reset requests to five per account per hour.
acceptance_criteria: Given five reset requests for an account in the preceding hour, when a sixth is submitted within that hour, then no additional reset link is issued for that account and the user-visible response remains the same generic response.
Given fewer than five reset requests for an account in the preceding hour, when another request is submitted, then it can be accepted within the limit.

requirements.statement: Issue a reset link for an accepted request for an existing account.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing synthetic account below its request limit, when its reset request is accepted, then a reset link for that account is recorded in the in-memory notification sink.

requirements.statement: Allow each reset link to complete a reset only once.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid reset link has already completed a password reset, when it is submitted again, then it cannot complete another reset.

requirements.statement: Expire reset links 30 minutes after issuance.
acceptance_criteria: Given an unused link issued less than 30 minutes ago, when it is submitted, then it remains eligible for a password reset.
Given an unused link issued 30 minutes ago or earlier, when it is submitted, then it cannot complete a password reset.

requirements.statement: Update an account password through an eligible reset link.
acceptance_criteria: Given an eligible unused link for a synthetic account, when its reset is completed with a new password, then that account's password is updated.

requirements.statement: Sign an account out of every active session on successful reset.
acceptance_criteria: Given an account has active sessions, when its password reset succeeds, then none of those sessions remains signed in.

requirements.statement: Notify the account owner after every successful password reset.
acceptance_criteria: Given an account's password reset succeeds, when completion is processed, then an owner-directed notification for that reset is recorded in the in-memory sink.

requirements.statement: Use synthetic accounts in the application.
acceptance_criteria: Given the application is exercised, when an account is needed for recovery, then it uses a synthetic account without requiring a production account integration.

requirements.statement: Record recovery notifications in an in-memory sink.
acceptance_criteria: Given a recovery notification is generated, when it is delivered, then it is available in an in-memory sink without requiring an external notification service.

requirements.statement: Run the application on Python 3.12 with Flask.
acceptance_criteria: Given Python 3.12 and the project dependencies, when the application runs, then its web behavior is served by Flask.

requirements.statement: Serve application pages as server-rendered HTML.
acceptance_criteria: Given a browser requests an application page, when Flask responds, then the page content is rendered on the server.

requirements.statement: Provide automated pytest coverage of the sign-in surface and recovery behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given the project test environment, when pytest runs, then automated tests check the sign-in surface and recovery behavior including requests, response equality, per-account limiting, links, reset completion, session sign-out where active sessions exist, and owner notification.

Given a reader opens the project documentation, when they look for production limitations, then it explains limitations of this small implementation, including synthetic accounts and in-memory notifications.
